additional_info.subject: RE: ID0416029-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2/R5 313059216002] Connector unavailable CRM:00921001659
additional_info.body:
Hey team,
Background: Charger uses Power saving mode.
It appears the charger shows as “available”.
Then the user either plugs in or sends a remote start to authenticate, during this time the charger is still preparing.
It appears the first session then “fails” as the connectors aren’t available, and this is only sent to the CPO when the user has already plugged in. CPO gets unavailable.
Would you please explain to us, how the user/CPO should use power saving mode?
It appears there needs to be some “delay” before they actually plug in.
With Kind Regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
Siemens Ltd.
Application Service Engineer
Phone: +61 499 701 794
Email: ferdinand.reisch@siemens.com
www.siemens.com.au/emobility

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0416029-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2/R5 313059216002] Connector unavailable CRM:00921001659
additional_info.body:
Hello Liz and Neil,
Reviewing some of the charging sessions that Sean conducted last Friday, it appears there is a similar behaviour (on CCS2).
At least from my analysis (minimum with Power saving mode), it appears there is a delayed “readiness” from the charger as it comes out of the power saving mode.
This occurred with Sean's charging sessions as well, when first plugged in, the connectors go "unavailable", which appears to fault/end that current session (session never started, but user wanted to start).
There is then a delay (based off logs ~20 seconds), after which the connectors are available again for use and then the session is able to take place as normal.
As the connectors become “unavailable” during the time, it might be that the LEDs go white (possibly even red, depending on how the vehicle reacts to this), which may cause the user to unplug.
I believe this happened with the user this morning, while on the session with Sean, he left the socket plugged in and the session was able to be restarted (noted with another remote start).
Is it possible to test out this series of operation on the charger?
I think it would help validate the theory and allow us to brainstorm some sequencing, while of course the global team validate and provide further suggestions.
I will also try to see if there is more detailed documentation around the Power Saving mode or operational behaviour globally.
With Kind Regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
Siemens Ltd.
Application Service Engineer
Email: ferdinand.reisch@siemens.com
www.siemens.com.au/emobility

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0416029-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2/R5 313059216002] Connector unavailable CRM:00921001659
additional_info.body:
Hello Ferdinand,
Thanks for the response.
If Power saving mode is activated and no charging processes are active, the main switch (-QA1) opens after 3 minutes and disconnects the power line (including the converters) from the mains.
Activate via the OCPP parameter PowerSavingModeSchedule. The parameter is configured in 24hours-clock. Use the same start and stop time if the power saving mode shall be activated all the time e. g. "00:00|00:00". The OCPP parameter IsPowerSavingModeActive shows if active or not. Feature is explained in the support document
Link
of chapter 3.18 of SICHARGE D operating instructions. Configuration parameters are listed in the Software Manual
Link
.
Regards,
Beerpal Singh
eMobility Support

additional_info.subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] RE: ID0416029-DC/Si-D/NZ-[Y2/R5 313059216002] Connector unavailable CRM:00921001659
additional_info.body:
Hi Ferdinand,
I can confirm this has occurred during onsite commissioning as well, I chalked it up to me being out of sequence with the remote OCPP command, but this makes more sense now.
A second start command within the 3 minute ‘non power saving window’ did start the charge correctly.
The pace that we were transitioning from inserting the plug into the vehicle and sending the start command was often greater then 30 seconds as we were busy checking the BESS units current draw response prior to starting the charge.
The side indicators go white, not red during this time (I will check and see if I have a video or some dates/times to back this up).
I also have seen that as the charger starts the charging process without checking for a vehicle first, some of our app users have inadvertently started a charging request whilst not being physically onsite. This was only discovered after I had contacted them to ask for feedback, they then admitted that they were not onsite.

Hey Neil,
Thanks for your time on the phone.
As we both discussed, while its good information to know that sometimes the QA1 does close after a reboot, it’s not really a solution to go forward with.
We will factor this into the site investigation, to be mindful of the fresh reboot, might have success, but needs to be checked after exiting power saving mode.
As for the discussion about the ELMS trip line.
I saw in the logs:
“ELMS -> SICHARGE, Trip Line activated, however safety relay not tripped”
According to the manual:
So it appears to be inverted logic, e.g. no Trip = True, Tripped = False.
It appears from the logs, this warning only comes up as the external stop is disengaged from the PLC, I don’t see a warning when it is engaged.
Might be worth checking if this bit is being controlled from the PLC?
